newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds paralysed by U.S. uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds paralysed by U.S. uncertainty.

text.p: *Australian bonds held to a tight trading range, after a technical rebound in after hours trading on Friday, as concerns over the U.S. market remained the overshadowing factor.
*Local current account deficit widens again in November.

Australian bonds held to a tight trading range, after a technical rebound in after hours trading on Friday, as concerns over U.S. Treasuries remained the overshadowing factor ahead of some key data there this week.

Recent U.S. data suggesting that the economy has taken off has renewed fears that the Federal Reserve may step in to tighten policy, and is keeping the local market very much on its guard, traders said.
The key test for the U.S., and global debt markets generally, will be Thursday's release of the December PPI followed by non-farm payrolls on Friday.

This caution limited the response to today's first major domestic report of the year, the November balance of payments, which showed the current account deficit widening to A$1.923 billion from a revised A$1.807 billion shortfall in October.

"The fifth consecutive increase in the current account deficit cannot be trivialised. We are still not giving up on our A$20 billion forecast for all of 1996/97, although there is more upside risk than downside risk to this forecast now," said Chris Caton, chief economist at Bankers Trust Australia.
ANZ's job ads series for December was released at the same time, falling 3.9 percent after a previous 2.1 percent rise.
The data was seen negating the impact of the balance of payments report, although the series tends to be volatile around the Christmas period, analysts noted.

"The current level of the ANZ job ads series remains consistent with around 11,000 new jobs on average," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said. "Although weak and insufficient to sustainably lower the unemployment rate, they still suggest an annual pace of employment growth of 1.6 percent."
Meanwhile, economists' median forecasts for Tuesday's release of November retail trade centre on a 1.0 percent rise, while building approvals are see down 2.0 percent.

The firmer, albeit thinly traded, stance of the local market saw the long-end outperform the dollar bloc and pare some of Friday's sharp yield spread widening. U.S. yields were marginally lower in Tokyo trading after ending little changed in New York, where Fed worries saw an initial advance evaporate.

Support at 92.210 on the 10-year bond survived Friday's test. This level represents a peak seen in August 1996 prior to slipping to 91.670 in early September. Resistance is seen at 92.340, the broken 50 percent retracement line of the September to December rally. -- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
